facts.text: The traj_follow node creates the q_ref service of type Ref.
The traj_follow node creates a joint_states subscription with sensor_msgs/JointState and a publisher for std_msgs/Float64MultiArray on /forward_effort_controller/commands.
The traj_follow listener reads positions 0..2 and velocities 0..2, uses fixed gains 1, 1.5, 1 and 2.5, and computes tau1, tau2 and tau3 from qref1..3; tau3 adds a constant -9.8.
The q_ref callback assigns qref1, qref2 and qref3 from request fields a, b and c and returns qref1 in response field i.

The traj_follow constructor sets qref1, qref2 and qref3 to 0.0 and creates the q_ref service, the joint_states subscription and the effort publisher; it creates no other service, subscription or publisher.
The traj_follow listener publishes the computed efforts on /forward_effort_controller/commands at the end of every joint_states callback.

The control_velocity node creates the Forward_Velocity_Kinematics Fvel service and the Inverse_Velocity_Kinematics Ivel service, creates a joint_states subscription and a publisher for std_msgs/Float64MultiArray on /forward_effort_controller/commands.
The Ivel callback assigns ev1, ev2 and ev3 from request endeff_vel_x, endeff_vel_y and endeff_vel_z.
The control_velocity listener uses J_inv multiplied by the Ev globals to form desired_velocity and computes a PID effort on every joint_states message.
The Fvel callback computes end-effector velocities from the requested joint velocities and returns endeff_vel_x, endeff_vel_y and endeff_vel_z.

The control_velocity constructor initialises its globals and creates the Fvel and Ivel services, the joint_states subscription and the effort publisher; it creates no other service, subscription or publisher.
The control_velocity listener adds -9.8 to the joint3 effort and publishes the efforts on /forward_effort_controller/commands at the end of every joint_states callback.
The FK node creates a joint_states subscription with sensor_msgs/JointState and a publisher for the homogeneous matrix as a std_msgs/String on the relative topic h_mat.
The FK listener computes A1, A2, A3 and their product H, writes H into a four-line string and publishes it on h_mat.
The service_member_function node creates the Inverse_Kinematics service of type Ik.
The service_member_function IK callback assigns the five response fields from its four two-link solutions and the computed d3.

The py_srvcli console scripts run traj_follow for service and listener, control_velocity for control, and name a Velocity_Service module for vel; there is no console script for service_member_function.
The URDF declares joint1 and joint2 as continuous revolute joints and joint3 as a prismatic joint whose limit is lower -${height4-width}, upper 0, effort 1000 and velocity 0.2.
The ros2_control description declares position and velocity command interfaces at -10..10 and effort command interfaces at -100..100 for joint1, joint2 and joint3.

The rrbot_world launch includes Gazebo, starts controller_manager, spawns the joint state broadcaster, spawns forward_position_controller and forward_velocity_controller stopped, and spawns forward_effort_controller active.
The rrbot_world launch includes gazebo_ros's gazebo.launch.py with the rrbot world.
The rrbot_world launch starts a Node with package controller_manager and executable ros2_control_node, and passes robot_description and robot_controllers as its parameters.
The launch description starts gazebo, spawn_entity, the standalone controller_manager node, robot_state_publisher, the joint_state_broadcaster spawner and the delayed controller spawners.
The spawners name the controller manager /controller_manager.
The rrbot Gazebo description loads the gazebo_ros2_control plugin (libgazebo_ros2_control.so) with the gazebo_controllers.yaml parameters.
The rrbot ros2_control description uses the gazebo_ros2_control/GazeboSystem hardware plugin.
The controller_switch client creates /controller_manager/switch_controller and sets activate_controllers to forward_velocity_controller and deactivate_controllers to forward_position_controller.
The gazebo_controllers configuration declares forward_effort_controller as a forward_command_controller/ForwardCommandController for joint1, joint2 and joint3 with the effort interface.
The README runs ros2 run FK listener.
The README runs py_srvcli service and calls q_ref, and runs py_srvcli control and calls Forward_Velocity_Kinematics and Inverse_Velocity_Kinematics.
The README calls Inverse_Kinematics after ros2 run py_srvcli service.
The py_srvcli package.xml declares Apache License 2.0.
The FK package manifest still contains the placeholder license text TODO: License declaration.
The ikinterface package manifest still contains the placeholder license text TODO: License declaration.
The rrbot_gazebo package.xml declares BSD.
gazebo.launch.py includes gzserver.launch.py unless its server argument is false.
gzserver.launch.py adds the init and factory gazebo_ros system plugins to the server command.
gzserver.launch.py defaults its init and factory arguments to true.
The init plugin takes the shared gazebo_ros node from gazebo_ros::Node::Get().
gazebo_ros::Node::Get creates the shared node named gazebo with an empty namespace.
The gazebo_ros executor spins its nodes on a thread of its own.
The init plugin creates the pause_physics and unpause_physics services with the std_srvs::srv::Empty type.
OnPause calls world_->SetPaused(true).
OnUnpause calls world_->SetPaused(false).
The init plugin publishes the simulation clock from a world-update-begin callback.
The factory plugin creates the get_model_list service with the gazebo_msgs::srv::GetModelList type.
GetModelList sets header.stamp to the world's simulation time, lists the model names and sets success true.
The GetModelList response documents header.stamp as the simulation time when the data was collected.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
The gazebo_ros2_control plugin creates its controller manager node with the name controller_manager.
The gazebo_ros2_control plugin calls GazeboSystem::initSim with the model the plugin is loaded for.
gazebo_ros2_control spins its controller manager's executor on a thread of its own.
gazebo_ros2_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros2_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and writes their commands to the joints.
GazeboSystem::initSim creates the system's private data and stores the parent model.
GazeboSystem::write reads the simulation time from the parent model's world.

determinism.notes: Event-driven rosbridge fake with canned service values and topic samples; no physics step, controller loop, effort integration or wall-clock pacing

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free recording transport for the pinned ROS 2 services and topics (no Gazebo)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free analytic contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic: it runs no Gazebo physics, ros2_control/controller_manager, traj_follow PD loop, control_velocity PID loop or FK/IK node
every joint position, velocity, effort, homogeneous matrix and service answer in the fake is a # placeholder; a live deployment must receive them from the operator's ROS graph

the effort publication is transmission-only: the receipt says published=true and confirmed=false and reports the three efforts it handed to rosbridge (the transmitted request, not a measurement); it does not prove that a controller consumed the message, that the simulated arm moved or that it stopped; the fake shifts its placeholder joint positions by a tiny amount on a publication, and that shift is not physics or motion evidence

the high-level q_ref and Ivel services are not bound: their responses expose no success/failure field (traj_follow.py:72, control_velocity.py:239-241) and the RosDriver requires an application predicate for an effectful service; binding them as observations would hide their motion effect

the Inverse_Kinematics service is not bound: setup.py does not register service_member_function (the service and listener entries run traj_follow), so the README's ros2 run command does not advertise that endpoint, and its inputs have no stated bounds

the clone exposes no acknowledged stop, pause, cancel or safe-state service/action, and deactivating the effort controller with /controller_manager/switch_controller is not presented as a safe state; the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause, confirmed by the E1 stall read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that /pause_physics sets and a sim-time stamp that /get_model_list reports and that advances on every answer unless paused; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

a frozen get_model_list stamp is also what a hung but unpaused gzserver shows (nothing advances then either); a GUI step or a WorldControl multi_step between the two samples fails the check (fails closed); the e-stop declares estop_latency_ms 1500 because the pause (400 ms), two read-backs (300 ms each) and the 250 ms interval exceed the default 1000 ms budget

no unpause is offered: traj_follow and control_velocity publish a new effort on every joint_states message and add a constant -9.8 to the joint3 effort (traj_follow.py:25-66, control_velocity.py:65-164), so this package cannot clear the effort the controller applies when the world resumes, and a zero effort is not what the upstream controllers command; the operator recovers outside MHS (stop traj_follow and control_velocity, decide the command on /forward_effort_controller/commands, then the Gazebo GUI play button or ros2 service call /unpause_physics)

rrbot_world.launch.py starts a standalone controller_manager ros2_control_node (rrbot_world.launch.py:69-75) beside the controller manager that the gazebo_ros2_control plugin creates inside gzserver under the same name; only the plugin gives a GazeboSystem a model (gazebo_ros2_control_plugin.cpp:337-346, gazebo_system.cpp:134-144, 818-825), so the standalone node cannot act on the Gazebo world, but whether it runs, fails or publishes /joint_states on the system clock while the world is paused is not settled by the source; the device resource therefore reads no topic, and the explicit joint-state read may still answer while the world is paused (the fake's wall_clock_joint_states switch)

while paused, the gzserver controller manager's joint_state_broadcaster and /clock come only from world updates; the fake silences /joint_states while paused unless its wall_clock_joint_states switch is set

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI, a WorldControl message (World.cc:1630-1639) or any ROS 2 client of /unpause_physics, and World::Step still advances sim time and calls Update while paused when a step is pending or a reset is due (World.cc:835-841), which makes gazebo_ros2_control write joint commands (gazebo_ros2_control_plugin.cpp:433-436); the two-sample stall is the whole confirmation window, and safety_status returns that cached confirmation and does not call /get_model_list again (RosBridge.safety_status, mhs/bridge/ros.py:2227-2232)

the deployment's gazebo_ros, gazebo_ros2_control and Gazebo must be the pinned 3.9.0, 0.4.12 and 11.15.1 releases the companion citations name; the clone's Humble and Gazebo 11 evidence is its committed colcon artifacts (install/setup.bash:22, build/rrbot_description/colcon_command_prefix_build.sh.env:13, 37), and rosbridge cannot read the deployed versions

NOT COVERED: Gazebo physics and collisions, controller_manager/ros2_control, the real PD/PID timing and gains, joint-limit enforcement, the q_ref and Ivel control paths, the IK service, /tf, and hardware

safe_state.description: Two /get_model_list answers 250 ms apart share header.stamp in that confirmation window: a frozen sim time, not a measured standstill. A paused World::Step still updates when a step is pending or a reset is due (World.cc:835-841; WorldControl :1630-1639), and gazebo_ros2_control writes joint commands (gazebo_ros2_control_plugin.cpp:433-436). safety_status returns that cached confirmation. No unpause is offered: stop traj_follow and control_velocity, decide the effort, and unpause outside MHS.
